title: the shim names the instance it would take, and refuses a name already live
intention: A launcher that wants another instance of a device asks the shim 'which instance would you take?': shim.name_instance(device) answers the lowest free number through address.next_free_instance, and name_instance(device, requested) refuses a number that already exists. It is callable without a running instance (a module-level function), because the asker is the launcher, not a client of instance 0. It names; it launches nothing.
why: Akien, outline 5.3.5.2.2 (said 2026-11-13): 'the launcher has to ask the shim to create the instance, and so it's the shim's job to say ... we have a cc_0 instance, so I'll launch it with cc_1'. The launcher asks, the shim names, the launcher launches (orchestrator ruling 2026-11-13); the shim has no per-instance launch path (shim.py:1288 starts the one instance it is), so this ticket is the naming half only. Refusing an explicit live name is CC's reading of Q#93, not his words. Split from b38af5fd1852 under RULE 1; depends on 0f7a8cada1ca.
traces_to: CP1 (an unroutable duplicate name must be impossible, not tolerated) and outline 5.3.5.2.
how: Add shim.name_instance(device_id, requested=None, roots=None) -> int. No requested: address.next_free_instance(device_id, roots). requested: return it if address.instances(device_id, roots) does not hold it, else raise InstanceTaken naming it (CC's reading of Q#93). Reads instance folders only through the address tool (0f7a8cada1ca), never by globbing devices/<device>/ in shim.py. One proof over a scratch roots dict, one tooth per clause.

clauses.claim: name_instance(device) with no requested number returns the lowest instance number the device does not have ([0, 2] gives 1, none gives 0), callable without a running shim or instance

name_instance(device, requested) returns requested when it is free and raises InstanceTaken naming it when that instance already exists, so two never share a name (CC's reading of Q#93, not Akien's words)

decisions.text: D1: a module-level name_instance in shim.py that reads instances only through cairn.tools.base.address; InstanceTaken for an explicit live name.
D2: one proof over a scratch roots dict, one tooth per clause; red first. Needs 0f7a8cada1ca on main first (address.instances / next_free_instance).

out: the launcher and the dispatcher (they ask and launch)
a device declaring whether it may have more than one instance (follow-on, not built)

measured.saw: cairn/tools/base/shim.py declares a 'start' verb ('wakes the device instance's process') and a presence of ONLINE/OFFLINE (lines ~59-60); no next-instance rule found by grep of its instance handling

Narrowed by the orchestrator's ruling: shim.py:1288 'start' starts the one instance the shim already is (diagnostic_instance, default 0), and nothing in the shim launches an instance N; so the shim can name an instance but not launch one. superclaude (ae4d581be071, open-62a7f29771e6 'b, next free instance') already does next-free for cc in bash; bin/cairn routes cairn <device>[.<instance>].
